requirements: mmgr must be a valid, initialized HPDF memory manager handle.
xref must be a valid HPDF cross-reference (document) handle associated with mmgr.
rect must be a valid on-page rectangle; precise constraints are not documented here.
text, if non-null, must point to a null-terminated string; whether null/empty is allowed is not specified.
encoder must be a valid HPDF_Encoder if text is provided; exact requirements are not stated.
subtype must be a valid HPDF_AnnotType value corresponding to a markup subtype; exact accepted values are not specified.
Returns an HPDF_Annotation handle on success; error handling details are not provided here.

functions.name: HPDF_PopupAnnot_New
functions.signature: HPDF_Annotation HPDF_PopupAnnot_New(HPDF_MMgr mmgr, HPDF_Xref xref, HPDF_Rect rect, HPDF_Annotation parent);
functions.description: Creates a popup annotation associated with a parent annotation. The popup occupies the given rectangle and is linked to the provided parent annotation.
requirements: mmgr must be a valid, initialized HPDF memory manager handle.
xref must be a valid HPDF cross-reference (document) handle associated with mmgr.
rect must be a valid on-page rectangle; exact constraints are not documented here.
parent must be a valid HPDF_Annotation handle representing the annotation that owns/displays the popup; null acceptability is not documented.
Returns an HPDF_Annotation handle on success; error handling is not documented here.

functions.name: HPDF_StampAnnot_New
functions.signature: HPDF_Annotation HPDF_StampAnnot_New(HPDF_MMgr mmgr, HPDF_Xref xref, HPDF_Rect rect, HPDF_StampAnnotName name, const char *text, HPDF_Encoder encoder);
functions.description: Creates a stamp annotation with a predefined stamp name and optional text, using the provided text encoder. The annotation occupies the specified rectangle.
requirements: mmgr must be a valid, initialized HPDF memory manager handle.
xref must be a valid HPDF cross-reference (document) handle associated with mmgr.
rect must be a valid on-page rectangle; precise constraints are not documented here.
name must be a valid HPDF_StampAnnotName value; acceptable values are not listed here.
text, if provided, must be a null-terminated C string; whether it can be null/empty is not specified.
encoder must be a valid HPDF_Encoder if text is used; exact requirements are not stated.
Returns an HPDF_Annotation handle on success; error handling approach is not documented here.

functions.name: HPDF_ProjectionAnnot_New
functions.signature: HPDF_Annotation HPDF_ProjectionAnnot_New(HPDF_MMgr mmgr, HPDF_Xref xref, HPDF_Rect rect, const char *text, HPDF_Encoder encoder);
functions.description: Creates a projection annotation with optional text content encoded via the provided encoder. The annotation occupies the specified rectangle. Specific behavior of a "projection" annotation is not described in this header.
requirements: mmgr must be a valid, initialized HPDF memory manager handle.
xref must be a valid HPDF cross-reference (document) handle associated with mmgr.
rect must be a valid on-page rectangle; precise constraints are not documented here.
text, if provided, must be a null-terminated C string; whether null/empty is allowed is not specified.
encoder must be a valid HPDF_Encoder if text is used; exact requirements are not stated.
Returns an HPDF_Annotation handle on success; error handling details are not provided here.

functions.name: HPDF_Annotation_Validate
functions.description: Validates an annotation handle. Returns a boolean indicating whether the provided HPDF_Annotation is valid. Additional validation semantics are not described in this header.
requirements: annot must be an HPDF_Annotation handle; may be null or invalid to test, but behavior for null is not specified here.
Returns HPDF_BOOL indicating validity; the meaning of true/false follows library conventions but is not detailed here.

functions.name: HPDF_Catalog_New
functions.description: Creates and returns a new PDF Catalog dictionary object for a document, using the provided memory manager and cross-reference (xref). Typically called during document initialization to set up the root Catalog. Returns a handle to the catalog (or an invalid/null handle on failure).
requirements: catalog is created for a document managed by the provided HPDF_MMgr and HPDF_Xref
mmgr must be a valid, initialized memory manager handle
xref must be a valid, initialized cross-reference table handle
callers should check the returned handle for validity before further use
must be called before attempting to query or modify catalog properties

functions.name: HPDF_Catalog_GetNames
functions.description: Retrieves the Names dictionary associated with the Catalog. Use this to access named destinations and other name trees in the document.
requirements: catalog must be a valid Catalog handle created for the document
may return a null/invalid handle if a Names dictionary has not been set

functions.name: HPDF_Catalog_SetNames
functions.description: Associates a Names dictionary with the Catalog. Intended to install the document’s name trees (e.g., named destinations). Returns an HPDF_STATUS indicating success or failure.
requirements: catalog must be a valid Catalog handle
dict must be a valid Names dictionary object
dict should belong to the same document/xref as catalog
callers must check the returned HPDF_STATUS for errors

functions.name: HPDF_Catalog_GetRoot
functions.description: Returns the document’s root Pages node from the Catalog. Use this to access the page tree starting point.
requirements: catalog must be a valid Catalog handle
returned handle may be null/invalid if the catalog is not properly initialized

functions.name: HPDF_Catalog_GetPageLayout
functions.description: Gets the document’s page layout setting (e.g., single page, one column, two column).
requirements: catalog must be a valid Catalog handle

functions.name: HPDF_Catalog_SetPageLayout
functions.description: Sets the document’s page layout displayed by viewers. Returns HPDF_STATUS indicating success or failure.
requirements: catalog must be a valid Catalog handle
layout must be a valid HPDF_PageLayout enumeration value
callers must check the returned HPDF_STATUS for errors

functions.name: HPDF_Catalog_GetPageMode
functions.description: Gets the document’s initial page mode (e.g., show outlines, thumbnails, or full screen) stored in the Catalog.
requirements: catalog must be a valid Catalog handle

functions.name: HPDF_Catalog_SetPageMode
functions.description: Sets the document’s initial page mode for PDF viewers. Returns HPDF_STATUS indicating success or failure.
requirements: catalog must be a valid Catalog handle
mode must be a valid HPDF_PageMode enumeration value
callers must check the returned HPDF_STATUS for errors

functions.name: HPDF_Catalog_SetOpenAction
functions.description: Sets the document’s open action (destination to display when the document is opened). Returns HPDF_STATUS indicating success or failure.
requirements: catalog must be a valid Catalog handle
open_action must be a valid HPDF_Destination handle
open_action should belong to the same document/xref as catalog
callers must check the returned HPDF_STATUS for errors

functions.name: HPDF_Catalog_AddPageLabel
functions.signature: HPDF_STATUS HPDF_Catalog_AddPageLabel(HPDF_Catalog catalog, HPDF_UINT page_num, HPDF_Dict page_label);
functions.description: Adds or updates a page label entry starting at the specified page number using the provided page label dictionary. Returns HPDF_STATUS indicating success or failure.
requirements: catalog must be a valid Catalog handle
page_label must be a valid dictionary containing a proper PageLabel definition
page_num must reference a valid page index within the document (exact indexing base is unknown from this header)
page_label should belong to the same document/xref as catalog
callers must check the returned HPDF_STATUS for errors

functions.name: HPDF_Catalog_GetViewerPreference
functions.description: Gets the viewer preference flags from the Catalog as a bitmask value.
requirements: catalog must be a valid Catalog handle
returned value is a bitmask of viewer preference flags; specific bits are not defined in this header

functions.name: HPDF_Catalog_SetViewerPreference
functions.description: Sets viewer preference flags in the Catalog using the provided bitmask. Returns HPDF_STATUS indicating success or failure.
requirements: catalog must be a valid Catalog handle
value should be a bitmask composed of supported viewer preference flags (exact flags not defined in this header)
callers must check the returned HPDF_STATUS for errors

functions.name: HPDF_Catalog_Validate
functions.description: Validates the Catalog object’s internal structure and required entries. Returns HPDF_TRUE if the catalog is valid, otherwise HPDF_FALSE.
requirements: catalog must be a valid Catalog handle

functions.name: fopen
functions.description: Opens a file and returns a stream associated with the given filename using the specified open mode (e.g., "r", "w", "a", optionally with "b", "+"). Use the returned FILE* for subsequent I/O and close it with fclose(). Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: filename must point to a valid, null-terminated string identifying a file path.
mode must be a valid, null-terminated C file open mode string (e.g., "r", "w", "a", and variants with "+" and/or "b").
The returned FILE* must be checked for NULL before use to handle open failures.
Each successfully opened stream must be closed exactly once with fclose().
The stream must not be used after it has been closed.

functions.name: fclose
functions.description: Closes an open file stream, flushing any unwritten data and releasing associated resources. Returns 0 on success, EOF on error.
requirements: stream must be a valid pointer to an open FILE obtained from fopen, freopen, or tmpfile.
Do not use stream after fclose returns (regardless of success).
Call exactly once per successfully opened stream.

functions.name: fread
functions.signature: size_t fread(void *ptr, size_t size, size_t nmemb, FILE *stream);
functions.description: Reads up to nmemb items of data, each of size bytes, from the stream into the buffer ptr. Returns the number of items successfully read, which may be less than requested on EOF or error.
requirements: ptr must point to a writable buffer of at least size*nmemb bytes unless size==0 or nmemb==0.
stream must be a valid readable FILE*; the file must be opened in a mode permitting reading.
Caller should examine the return value and use ferror/feof to distinguish error from EOF when fewer than nmemb items are read.
Behavior is undefined if ptr is NULL and size*nmemb > 0.

functions.name: fwrite
functions.signature: size_t fwrite(const void *ptr, size_t size, size_t nmemb, FILE *stream);
functions.description: Writes nmemb items of data, each of size bytes, from the buffer ptr to the stream. Returns the number of items successfully written, which may be less than requested on error.
requirements: ptr must point to a readable buffer of at least size*nmemb bytes unless size==0 or nmemb==0.
stream must be a valid writable FILE*; the file must be opened in a mode permitting writing.
Caller must check the return value; fewer than nmemb indicates a write error (use ferror to diagnose).
Behavior is undefined if ptr is NULL and size*nmemb > 0.

functions.name: fflush
functions.description: Flushes the output buffer of the specified stream, writing any buffered data to the underlying file. If stream is NULL, flushes all open output streams. Returns 0 on success, EOF on error.
requirements: stream must be either NULL or a valid pointer to an open output stream.
Only meaningful for output or update streams; calling on input-only streams is implementation-defined.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: fseek
functions.signature: int fseek(FILE *stream, long offset, int whence);
functions.description: Repositions the file position indicator for stream to a new location determined by offset and whence (SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR, SEEK_END). Returns 0 on success, nonzero on error.
requirements: stream must be a valid pointer to an open, seekable FILE.
whence must be one of SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR, or SEEK_END.
After switching between reading and writing on an update stream, a positioning function (such as fseek or fflush) must be called before the next operation.
Large files may exceed the range of long; use fseeko/ftello where available if needed.
Caller must check the return value; nonzero indicates failure.

functions.name: ftell
functions.description: Returns the current file position indicator for stream as a long, or -1L on error.
requirements: stream must be a valid pointer to an open, seekable FILE.
Caller must check for a return value of -1L to detect errors.
For very large files, long may be insufficient; use ftello where available.

functions.name: feof
functions.description: Tests the end-of-file indicator for stream. Returns nonzero if EOF is set, zero otherwise.
requirements: stream must be a valid pointer to an open FILE.
Only indicates whether the EOF indicator is set; it does not attempt to read. Use in conjunction with fread/fgetc return values.

functions.name: ferror
functions.description: Tests the error indicator for stream. Returns nonzero if an I/O error has occurred on the stream, zero otherwise.
requirements: stream must be a valid pointer to an open FILE.
Clear error and EOF indicators with clearerr(stream) if needed.

functions.name: malloc
functions.description: Allocates size bytes of uninitialized storage and returns a pointer to the allocated memory, or NULL if the allocation fails or if size is zero and the implementation returns NULL for zero-sized allocation.
requirements: size must be the number of bytes to allocate; zero is allowed but may return NULL or a unique pointer depending on the implementation.
The returned pointer must be checked for NULL before use.
Memory returned must be released with free (or a compatible deallocation function) exactly once.
Do not read or write beyond the allocated size; contents are indeterminate.

functions.name: free
functions.description: Deallocates the memory block pointed to by ptr that was previously allocated by malloc/calloc/realloc/aligned allocation. Does nothing if ptr is NULL.
requirements: ptr must be either NULL or a pointer previously returned by a compatible allocation function and not yet freed.
Each allocated block must be freed exactly once; double-free is undefined behavior.
Do not use ptr after it has been freed.

functions.name: time
functions.description: Returns the current calendar time as a time_t value. If t is non-NULL, also stores the result in *t. Returns (time_t)-1 on error.
requirements: t may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to writable storage for a time_t.
Caller should check for return value (time_t)-1 to detect errors.

functions.name: printf
functions.description: Writes formatted output to stdout according to the format string and the additional arguments. Returns the number of characters printed (excluding the null terminator), or a negative value on error.
requirements: format must point to a valid null-terminated format string.
The variadic arguments must match the format specifiers in type and number; mismatches cause undefined behavior.
Caller should check the return value for a negative error indication.

functions.name: sin
functions.description: Computes the sine of x, where x is in radians. Returns the sine as a double.
requirements: x is interpreted in radians.
Domain errors or special values (e.g., NaN, infinity) follow the C math library’s error handling; caller should be prepared for NaN results for invalid inputs.

functions.name: cos
functions.description: Computes the cosine of x, where x is in radians. Returns the cosine as a double.
requirements: x is interpreted in radians.
Domain errors or special values (e.g., NaN, infinity) follow the C math library’s error handling; caller should be prepared for NaN results for invalid inputs.

functions.name: HPDF_Destination_New
functions.signature: HPDF_Destination HPDF_Destination_New(HPDF_MMgr mmgr, HPDF_Page target, HPDF_Xref xref);
functions.description: Creates a new PDF destination object associated with a given target page. Destinations in libharu are used to define view positions for links, outlines, or open actions. Typical usage is to create a destination for an existing page and then attach it to an annotation or outline entry. Specific view/zoom settings are configured elsewhere on the destination object; this function only allocates/initializes the destination bound to the target page. Detailed failure modes and ownership/lifetime rules are not documented in this header and are therefore unknown.
requirements: mmgr must be a valid HPDF_MMgr (memory manager) obtained from the library and valid for the duration of the call.
target must be a valid HPDF_Page created by the library; it should refer to a page of the current document/context.
xref must be a valid HPDF_Xref belonging to the same document/context as the target page.
All handles (mmgr, target, xref) must be initialized and not previously freed or otherwise invalidated.
Caller should check the returned HPDF_Destination before further use; exact error indication semantics (e.g., NULL on failure) are unknown from this header.

functions.name: HPDF_Destination_Validate
functions.description: Validates a destination handle, returning a boolean that indicates whether the destination object is structurally valid/usable. Typical usage is to check a destination returned from creation or loaded from an object before applying further operations (e.g., setting view parameters or attaching to links/outlines). Exact validation criteria are not specified in this header.
requirements: dst should be a destination handle (HPDF_Destination) obtained from the library.
If the function returns false, the caller must treat the destination as invalid and avoid further use with API calls that require a valid destination.
The acceptance of a null/invalid handle is unknown; callers should be prepared for false to be returned in such cases.

functions.name: HPDF_Doc_FindEncoder
functions.signature: HPDF_Encoder HPDF_Doc_FindEncoder(HPDF_Doc pdf, const char* encoding_name);
functions.description: Looks up and returns an encoder object by name within the given PDF document context. Typically used to obtain a character encoding to be applied to text or fonts. Returns an encoder handle associated with the document; exact error/return semantics are unknown from this header.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle
encoding_name should be a valid, null-terminated C string
The requested encoder is expected to be registered/available in the document (whether built-in or previously registered); otherwise behavior/return value is unknown
The returned HPDF_Encoder, if non-null, is used only with the same HPDF_Doc

functions.name: HPDF_Doc_FindFontDef
functions.signature: HPDF_FontDef HPDF_Doc_FindFontDef(HPDF_Doc pdf, const char* font_name);
functions.description: Finds a font definition by name within the document’s font definition list. Used when you need access to the underlying font metrics/definition. Exact behavior on missing fonts is not specified in this header.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle
font_name should be a valid, null-terminated C string
The font definition should be available in the document (predefined or previously registered); otherwise behavior/return value is unknown
Use the returned HPDF_FontDef only within the same HPDF_Doc

functions.name: HPDF_Doc_FindFont
functions.signature: HPDF_Font HPDF_Doc_FindFont(HPDF_Doc pdf, const char* font_name, const char* encoding_name);
functions.description: Retrieves a font object in the document for the given font and encoding names. Typically used before setting the font on a page or content stream. The exact error/return semantics are not specified here.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle
font_name should be a valid, null-terminated C string
encoding_name should be a valid, null-terminated C string
The specified font and encoder must be available/compatible within the document; otherwise behavior/return value is unknown
Use the returned HPDF_Font only with objects belonging to the same HPDF_Doc

functions.name: HPDF_Doc_Validate
functions.description: Validates internal state of the document. Intended to check whether the HPDF_Doc is in a consistent/usable state. Exact validation criteria and return semantics beyond boolean are not detailed in this header.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle

functions.name: HPDF_Doc_GetCurrentPages
functions.description: Returns the current HPDF_Pages node associated with the document (the current page tree/context). Useful when adding pages or modifying the current pages container. Behavior if no current pages exist is not specified here.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle
Use the returned HPDF_Pages only with the same HPDF_Doc

functions.name: HPDF_Doc_AddPagesTo
functions.description: Creates a new HPDF_Pages node and adds it under the specified parent pages node. Returns the newly added pages node. Details on insertion position or error behavior are not specified here.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle
parent must be a valid HPDF_Pages that belongs to the same HPDF_Doc
Use the returned HPDF_Pages only with the same HPDF_Doc

functions.name: HPDF_Doc_SetCurrentPages
functions.description: Sets the document’s current pages node to the provided pages handle. Typically used to change the active page tree context before adding pages. Returns an HPDF_STATUS indicating success or failure; specific codes are not provided here.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle
pages must be a valid HPDF_Pages that belongs to the same HPDF_Doc
Caller should check the returned HPDF_STATUS for success/failure; exact status values are unknown

functions.name: HPDF_Doc_SetCurrentPage
functions.description: Sets the document’s current page to the provided page handle. Useful to switch which page subsequent drawing operations target. Returns an HPDF_STATUS; exact status codes and side effects are not specified here.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle
page must be a valid HPDF_Page that belongs to the same HPDF_Doc
Caller should check the returned HPDF_STATUS for success/failure; exact status values are unknown

functions.name: HPDF_GetFontDef
functions.signature: HPDF_FontDef HPDF_GetFontDef(HPDF_Doc pdf, const char* font_name);
functions.description: Retrieves a font definition by name from the document, similar to HPDF_Doc_FindFontDef. Used to obtain access to font metrics/definition. Behavior when the font definition is not available is not specified here.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle
font_name should be a valid, null-terminated C string
Use the returned HPDF_FontDef only with the same HPDF_Doc

functions.name: HPDF_Doc_RegisterFontDef
functions.description: Registers a font definition object with the document so it can be used for creating fonts. Returns an HPDF_STATUS indicating success or failure; detailed error codes are not provided here.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle
fontdef must be a valid HPDF_FontDef, properly initialized by the library before registration
fontdef should be compatible with this document; cross-document reuse is not supported unless explicitly allowed (not specified here)
Caller should check the returned HPDF_STATUS for success/failure; exact status values are unknown

functions.name: HPDF_Doc_RegisterEncoder
functions.description: Registers an encoder object with the document so that it can be referenced by name and used for text encoding. Returns an HPDF_STATUS; specific error codes are not given here.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle
encoder must be a valid HPDF_Encoder, properly initialized by the library before registration
encoder should be compatible with this document; cross-document reuse is not supported unless explicitly allowed (not specified here)
Caller should check the returned HPDF_STATUS for success/failure; exact status values are unknown

functions.name: HPDF_Doc_SetEncryptOn
functions.description: Enables encryption for the document. Typically called before writing encrypted content or saving the document. Returns an HPDF_STATUS; exact prerequisites and error codes are not described here.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle
There may be prerequisites (e.g., encryption settings) before enabling encryption, but they are unknown from this header
Caller should check the returned HPDF_STATUS for success/failure; exact status values are unknown

functions.name: HPDF_Doc_SetEncryptOff
functions.description: Disables encryption for the document. Returns an HPDF_STATUS; detailed behavior and side effects are not specified here.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle
Caller should check the returned HPDF_STATUS for success/failure; exact status values are unknown

functions.name: HPDF_Doc_PrepareEncryption
functions.description: Prepares the document for encryption, likely finalizing internal encryption structures before saving. Returns an HPDF_STATUS; exact timing and required prior calls are not specified in this header.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle
This function likely should be called after encryption has been configured, but exact ordering is unknown from this header
Caller should check the returned HPDF_STATUS for success/failure; exact status values are unknown

functions.name: HPDF_Encoder_Validate
functions.description: Checks that an HPDF_Encoder instance is valid/initialized and ready for use. Typically used to verify an encoder handle before encoding operations.
requirements: encoder must be a non-NULL HPDF_Encoder handle.
encoder should refer to an initialized encoder (created by a corresponding New function or provided by the library).
Return value is an HPDF_STATUS error code; callers should check for success/failure.

functions.name: HPDF_Encoder_SetParseText
functions.signature: void HPDF_Encoder_SetParseText (HPDF_Encoder encoder, HPDF_ParseText_Rec *state, const HPDF_BYTE *text, HPDF_UINT len);
functions.description: Initializes or updates a parse state for scanning text bytes with a given encoder. Sets the text buffer and its length into the supplied HPDF_ParseText_Rec.
requirements: encoder must be a non-NULL HPDF_Encoder handle.
state must be a non-NULL pointer to an HPDF_ParseText_Rec structure.
text must point to a buffer containing at least len bytes of readable data; len specifies the number of bytes to scan.
The state structure’s fields will be updated; caller must provide a writable HPDF_ParseText_Rec.

functions.name: HPDF_Encoder_ByteType
functions.description: Determines the type of the next byte(s) in the text being parsed for the specified encoder (e.g., lead/trail/unknown byte). Uses and advances the provided parse state.
requirements: encoder must be a non-NULL HPDF_Encoder handle.
state must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid HPDF_ParseText_Rec previously set via HPDF_Encoder_SetParseText.
The HPDF_ParseText_Rec must reference a valid text buffer; the function may read bytes within [state->index, state->len).

functions.name: HPDF_Encoder_ToUnicode
functions.description: Maps an encoder-specific code value to a Unicode code point using the encoder’s mapping tables.
requirements: encoder must be a non-NULL HPDF_Encoder handle.
code is an encoder code unit; valid range and behavior for unmapped codes are unknown from this header and may be encoder-specific.

functions.name: HPDF_Encoder_Free
functions.description: Releases resources associated with an HPDF_Encoder. Should be called when the encoder is no longer needed.
requirements: encoder must be either NULL or a valid HPDF_Encoder obtained from the library (e.g., a New function).
After this call, the encoder handle must not be reused.

functions.name: HPDF_BasicEncoder_New
functions.description: Creates a basic (single-byte) encoder for a named encoding (e.g., StandardEncoding, WinAnsiEncoding).
requirements: mmgr must be a valid memory manager handle (HPDF_MMgr).
encoding_name must be a non-NULL, supported encoding name string (e.g., one of the HPDF_ENCODING_* macros).
On failure, may return NULL; callers must check the return value before use.

functions.name: HPDF_BasicEncoder_Free
functions.description: Frees a basic encoder and its associated resources.
requirements: encoder must be either NULL or a valid HPDF_Encoder previously created by HPDF_BasicEncoder_New.
Do not use the encoder after freeing it.

functions.name: HPDF_BasicEncoder_Write
functions.description: Serializes the basic encoder’s data to the provided output stream (e.g., when writing a PDF).
requirements: encoder must be a non-NULL, initialized basic encoder.
out must be a valid HPDF_Stream capable of being written to.
Returns HPDF_STATUS; callers must check for success/failure.

functions.name: HPDF_BasicEncoder_ToUnicode
functions.description: Converts a single-byte code from a basic encoder to its corresponding Unicode code point.
requirements: encoder must be a non-NULL basic encoder handle.
code is a code unit in the encoder’s code space; valid range and mapping behavior for unmapped codes are not specified here.

functions.name: HPDF_CMapEncoder_New
functions.signature: HPDF_Encoder HPDF_CMapEncoder_New (HPDF_MMgr mmgr, char *name, HPDF_Encoder_Init_Func init_fn);
functions.description: Creates a CMap-based encoder (typically for multibyte/cid-keyed fonts), assigning it a name and an initialization callback to set up mappings/attributes.
requirements: mmgr must be a valid HPDF_MMgr.
name must be a non-NULL C string used to identify the encoder.
init_fn must be a valid initializer callback (HPDF_Encoder_Init_Func) that configures the encoder; the encoder may be unusable if initialization fails.
On failure, may return NULL; callers must check the return value before use.

functions.name: HPDF_CMapEncoder_InitAttr
functions.description: Initializes or resets the attribute block for a CMap encoder (e.g., code space, ranges, writing mode).
requirements: encoder must be a non-NULL CMap encoder handle.
Returns HPDF_STATUS; callers must check for success/failure before further use.

functions.name: HPDF_CMapEncoder_Free
functions.description: Frees a CMap encoder and its resources.
requirements: encoder must be either NULL or a valid HPDF_Encoder returned by HPDF_CMapEncoder_New.
Do not access the encoder after freeing it.

functions.name: HPDF_CMapEncoder_Write
functions.description: Writes the CMap encoder’s definition/mappings to the given output stream.
requirements: encoder must be a non-NULL, initialized CMap encoder.
out must be a valid HPDF_Stream that is writable.
Returns HPDF_STATUS; callers must check for success/failure.

functions.name: HPDF_CMapEncoder_ToUnicode
functions.description: Maps a CMap encoder code to a Unicode code point using the encoder’s Unicode mapping tables.
requirements: encoder must be a non-NULL CMap encoder handle.
code is a code unit; exact valid range and handling of unmapped codes are not specified here.

functions.name: HPDF_CMapEncoder_ToCID
functions.description: Maps an encoded code unit to a CID (Character ID) according to the CMap encoder’s CID mapping.
requirements: encoder must be a non-NULL CMap encoder handle.
code is a code unit; valid range and behavior for unmapped codes are unspecified here.
Callers should be prepared to handle unmapped or special return values; exact semantics are not described in this header.

functions.name: HPDF_CMapEncoder_SetParseText
functions.signature: HPDF_STATUS HPDF_CMapEncoder_SetParseText (HPDF_Encoder encoder, HPDF_ParseText_Rec *state, const HPDF_BYTE *text, HPDF_UINT len);
functions.description: Prepares a parse state for scanning multibyte text according to the CMap encoder, associating the text buffer and length with the state.
requirements: encoder must be a non-NULL CMap encoder handle.
state must be a non-NULL pointer to an HPDF_ParseText_Rec to be initialized/updated.
text must point to at least len bytes of readable data.
Returns HPDF_STATUS; callers must check for success/failure.

functions.name: HPDF_CMapEncoder_ByteType
functions.description: Determines the type of the next byte(s) for a CMap (possibly multibyte) sequence using the provided parse state.
requirements: encoder must be a non-NULL CMap encoder handle.
state must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid HPDF_ParseText_Rec set up via HPDF_CMapEncoder_SetParseText.
The state must reference a valid text buffer; function may read within [state->index, state->len).

functions.name: HPDF_CMapEncoder_AddCMap
functions.description: Adds a CID mapping range to the CMap encoder, mapping a contiguous range of codes to sequential CIDs starting at range.cid.
requirements: encoder must be a non-NULL CMap encoder handle.
range must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid HPDF_CidRange_Rec.
The semantic expectation is that range.from <= range.to and fields contain valid code/CID values; exact constraints are not specified here.
Returns HPDF_STATUS; callers must check for success/failure.

functions.name: HPDF_CMapEncoder_AddNotDefRange
functions.description: Adds a range of codes to be treated as .notdef (undefined) in the CMap encoder.
requirements: encoder must be a non-NULL CMap encoder handle.
range is passed by value and should contain valid from/to bounds and a cid field as required by library conventions; precise constraints are not specified here.
Returns HPDF_STATUS; callers must check for success/failure.

functions.name: HPDF_CMapEncoder_AddCodeSpaceRange
functions.description: Adds a code space range to the CMap encoder, defining valid byte-sequence bounds for encoded characters.
requirements: encoder must be a non-NULL CMap encoder handle.
range must specify valid bounds; exact constraints are not provided in this header.
Returns HPDF_STATUS; callers must check for success/failure.

functions.name: HPDF_CMapEncoder_SetUnicodeArray
functions.description: Supplies the CMap encoder with an array of code-to-Unicode mappings.
requirements: encoder must be a non-NULL CMap encoder handle.
array1 must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid array of HPDF_UnicodeMap_Rec entries. The array length/termination convention is not specified in this header and is library-defined (unknown here).

functions.name: HPDF_CMapEncoder_AddJWWLineHead
functions.description: Registers one or more JWW line-head codes for the CMap encoder (used for line-breaking rules in some East Asian encodings).
requirements: encoder must be a non-NULL CMap encoder handle.
code must be a non-NULL pointer to a sequence of HPDF_UINT16 codes. The sequence length/termination convention is not specified in this header (unknown).
Returns HPDF_STATUS; callers must check for success/failure.

functions.name: HPDF_Encoder_CheckJWWLineHead
functions.signature: HPDF_BOOL HPDF_Encoder_CheckJWWLineHead (HPDF_Encoder encoder, const HPDF_UINT16 code);
functions.description: Checks whether a given code is registered as a JWW line-head code for the specified encoder.
requirements: encoder must be a non-NULL encoder handle (typically a CMap encoder configured with JWW line-head data).
code is the code unit to check; valid range unspecified.

functions.name: HPDF_UnicodeToGlyphName
functions.description: Converts a Unicode code point to its PostScript glyph name if known, returning a pointer to a static or library-managed string.
requirements: unicode is a Unicode code point; valid range and handling for unmapped values are unspecified here.
Return may be NULL if the glyph name is unknown; caller should not modify or free the returned string.

functions.name: HPDF_GlyphNameToUnicode
functions.description: Converts a PostScript glyph name to its corresponding Unicode code point, if known.
requirements: glyph_name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string.
Behavior for unknown/invalid names is unspecified in this header; callers should handle a potential 'no mapping' return value.

functions.name: HPDF_MD5Init
functions.description: Initializes an MD5 context for a new digest computation. Call this before any HPDF_MD5Update calls and once per digest calculation; finalize with HPDF_MD5Final.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to an HPDF_MD5Context structure.
HPDF_MD5Init must be called before HPDF_MD5Update/HPDF_MD5Final for a given context.
Do not reuse a context for a new digest without reinitializing it with HPDF_MD5Init.

functions.name: HPDF_MD5Update
functions.signature: void HPDF_MD5Update(struct HPDF_MD5Context *ctx, const HPDF_BYTE *buf, HPDF_UINT32 len);
functions.description: Feeds a buffer of bytes into the ongoing MD5 digest represented by ctx. May be called multiple times to process data in chunks.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, previously-initialized HPDF_MD5Context (via HPDF_MD5Init).
If len > 0, buf must point to at least len readable bytes.
len may be zero to indicate no data; in that case buf need not be dereferenceable.

functions.name: HPDF_MD5Final
functions.description: Finalizes the MD5 digest for the given context and writes the 16-byte result to digest. After finalization, the context should be reinitialized before reuse.
requirements: digest must point to a writable buffer of at least 16 bytes.
ctx must be a valid HPDF_MD5Context that has been initialized with HPDF_MD5Init and optionally updated via HPDF_MD5Update.
Do not call HPDF_MD5Update on ctx after HPDF_MD5Final without reinitializing the context.

functions.name: HPDF_PadOrTruncatePasswd
functions.description: Pads or truncates the input password to the fixed length used by PDF encryption (HPDF_PASSWD_LEN, typically 32 bytes), writing the result into new_pwd. Used to normalize user/owner passwords before key generation. If documentation is missing, behavior for NULL pwd or non-ASCII bytes is unknown; callers should provide a standard C string.
requirements: pwd should be a valid, null-terminated C string; the function determines its length via C string semantics. Behavior for NULL pwd is unknown.
new_pwd must point to a writable buffer of at least HPDF_PASSWD_LEN bytes (32).
Input bytes outside the expected character set are not validated by this signature; caller is responsible for encoding/normalization if required.

functions.name: HPDF_Encrypt_Init
functions.description: Initializes an HPDF_Encrypt structure with default/initial state for subsequent encryption setup and operations.
requirements: attr must be a valid pointer to an HPDF_Encrypt_Rec structure to be initialized.
After initialization, set fields such as mode, key_len, passwords, permission, etc., as required before creating keys.
key_len must be a multiple of 8 and between 40 and 128 bits (as indicated by the struct comment) before key generation functions are used.

functions.name: HPDF_Encrypt_CreateUserKey
functions.description: Generates the encrypted user password key (user_key) inside the HPDF_Encrypt structure based on current settings (passwords, permissions, IDs, and key length). Typically called after initialization and password setup.
requirements: attr must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Encrypt instance (initialized via HPDF_Encrypt_Init).
attr->user_passwd must be set (padded/truncated) prior to calling; expected length is HPDF_PASSWD_LEN bytes.
attr->key_len must satisfy: multiple of 8 and between 40 and 128 (inclusive).

Other fields used in key generation (e.g., encrypt_id, permission) must be set according to the desired document settings before invocation. Exact dependencies are not documented here; consult implementation.

functions.name: HPDF_Encrypt_CreateOwnerKey
functions.description: Generates the encrypted owner password key (owner_key) inside the HPDF_Encrypt structure using the current passwords and parameters. Typically used alongside CreateUserKey during encryption setup.
requirements: attr must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Encrypt instance (initialized via HPDF_Encrypt_Init).
attr->owner_passwd and attr->user_passwd should be set (padded/truncated) prior to calling; expected length is HPDF_PASSWD_LEN bytes.
attr->key_len must satisfy: multiple of 8 and between 40 and 128 (inclusive).
Other fields used in key generation (e.g., encrypt_id, permission) must be set before invocation as required by the encryption algorithm; specifics are not documented here.

functions.name: HPDF_Encrypt_CreateEncryptionKey
functions.description: Derives and stores the document encryption key in the HPDF_Encrypt structure using the configured parameters (passwords, permission, ID, and key length). This key is later specialized per object via HPDF_Encrypt_InitKey.
requirements: attr must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Encrypt instance (HPDF_Encrypt_Init).
attr->key_len must be a multiple of 8 and between 40 and 128 bits.

Required prerequisite fields (e.g., owner_key, user_key, permission, encrypt_id) should be prepared according to the algorithm prior to this call; exact ordering dependencies are not explicitly documented.

functions.name: HPDF_Encrypt_InitKey
functions.signature: void HPDF_Encrypt_InitKey(HPDF_Encrypt attr, HPDF_UINT32 object_id, HPDF_UINT16 gen_no);
functions.description: Initializes the per-object encryption key/ARC4 state within attr for encrypting or decrypting a specific PDF object identified by object_id and generation number. Call this before encrypting/decrypting the data of that object.
requirements: attr must be a valid HPDF_Encrypt instance that has had its document encryption key derived (via HPDF_Encrypt_CreateEncryptionKey).
object_id is the target PDF object number; must be the correct ID for the object being processed. Range constraints are not specified; must fit in HPDF_UINT32.
gen_no is the generation number for the object; must fit in HPDF_UINT16.

functions.name: HPDF_Encrypt_Reset
functions.description: Resets the internal ARC4/encryption state in attr, typically clearing or reinitializing buffers/state before a new encryption sequence. Exact semantics are not documented; intended to prepare attr for subsequent operations.
requirements: attr must be a valid HPDF_Encrypt instance.

Should be called when a fresh encryption state is needed. Any required re-initialization (e.g., HPDF_Encrypt_Init or HPDF_Encrypt_CreateEncryptionKey) after reset is not specified; consult implementation.

functions.name: HPDF_Encrypt_CryptBuf
functions.signature: void HPDF_Encrypt_CryptBuf(HPDF_Encrypt attr, const HPDF_BYTE *src, HPDF_BYTE *dst, HPDF_UINT len);
functions.description: Encrypts or decrypts a buffer of length len bytes using the current per-object encryption state in attr, reading from src and writing the result to dst. Typically called after HPDF_Encrypt_InitKey for a given object.
requirements: attr must be a valid HPDF_Encrypt instance with per-object key/state initialized via HPDF_Encrypt_InitKey for the target object.
If len > 0, src must point to at least len readable bytes.
dst must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
Behavior for overlapping src and dst buffers is not documented; callers should avoid overlap unless confirmed safe.
len may be zero to perform no operation.

functions.name: HPDF_EncryptDict_New
functions.description: Creates and returns a new encryption dictionary object associated with the given memory manager and cross-reference table. Typically used when setting up document encryption prior to writing the PDF. Details of initialization are internal to libharu; the returned handle represents the /Encrypt dictionary.
requirements: mmgr must reference a valid, initialized HPDF memory manager (inferred from naming and typical libharu patterns).
xref must reference a valid, initialized cross-reference table object (inferred).
Caller must check the returned HPDF_EncryptDict for validity (i.e., non-NULL) before further use (inferred).

functions.name: HPDF_EncryptDict_CreateID
functions.signature: void HPDF_EncryptDict_CreateID(HPDF_EncryptDict dict, HPDF_Dict info, HPDF_Xref xref);
functions.description: Generates and assigns document ID entries relevant to encryption using the provided document info dictionary and cross-reference. Intended to set or update identifiers used in encryption processing. Exact ID format/placement is internal to libharu.
requirements: dict must be a valid encryption dictionary previously created (inferred).
info must be a valid document info dictionary (HPDF_Dict) associated with the current document (inferred).
xref must be a valid cross-reference table for the current document (inferred).
Function does not return a status; callers should assume it requires valid, non-NULL arguments to avoid undefined behavior (inferred).

functions.name: HPDF_EncryptDict_OnFree
functions.description: Cleanup hook invoked when an encryption dictionary (or related dictionary object) is being freed. Releases internal resources associated with the given dictionary. Typically used internally as an object finalizer.
requirements: obj must be a valid HPDF_Dict corresponding to an encryption dictionary or a dictionary configured to use this free callback (inferred).
Caller should only call this as part of the object lifecycle management, not arbitrarily (inferred).

functions.name: HPDF_EncryptDict_SetPassword
functions.signature: HPDF_STATUS HPDF_EncryptDict_SetPassword(HPDF_EncryptDict dict, const char *owner_passwd, const char *user_passwd);
functions.description: Sets the owner and user passwords for the encryption dictionary. Use prior to preparing/writing the document to configure encryption credentials. Returns an HPDF_STATUS code indicating success or failure.
requirements: dict must be a valid, initialized encryption dictionary (inferred).
owner_passwd is a pointer to a NUL-terminated string; constraints on length/encoding are unknown from this header (unknown specifics).
user_passwd is a pointer to a NUL-terminated string; constraints on length/encoding are unknown from this header (unknown specifics).
Caller must check the returned HPDF_STATUS and handle errors appropriately (inferred from status-returning convention).
If NULL passwords are not supported, passing NULL may cause an error; support for empty or NULL passwords is unknown (unknown specifics).

functions.name: HPDF_EncryptDict_Validate
functions.description: Validates the internal state of the encryption dictionary and returns a boolean indicating whether it is properly configured. Useful before preparing/saving the document.
requirements: dict must be a valid encryption dictionary handle (inferred).
Caller must check the returned HPDF_BOOL; true indicates valid, false indicates invalid (inferred from naming).

functions.name: HPDF_EncryptDict_Prepare
functions.signature: HPDF_STATUS HPDF_EncryptDict_Prepare(HPDF_EncryptDict dict, HPDF_Dict info, HPDF_Xref xref);
functions.description: Finalizes and prepares the encryption dictionary for inclusion in the document, using the document info and cross-reference context. Typically called after setting passwords and before writing the PDF to output. Returns an HPDF_STATUS code.
requirements: dict must be a valid encryption dictionary, typically with passwords already set if encryption is desired (inferred).
info must be a valid document info dictionary (HPDF_Dict) (inferred).
xref must be a valid cross-reference table (HPDF_Xref) (inferred).
Caller must check the returned HPDF_STATUS and not proceed on failure (inferred).
Call timing: should be invoked during document finalization prior to writing output (inferred from name).

functions.name: HPDF_EncryptDict_GetAttr
functions.description: Returns the underlying HPDF_Encrypt attribute/object associated with the encryption dictionary. Provides access to low-level encryption parameters/state for internal or advanced use.
requirements: dict must be a valid encryption dictionary (inferred).
Returned HPDF_Encrypt must be treated as read-only unless documented otherwise; exact mutability and lifetime are unknown (unknown specifics).

functions.name: HPDF_Error_Init
functions.description: Initializes an HPDF_Error record for use with the libharu error subsystem. Sets up the error handler (defaults are used by the library) and stores user_data to identify the throwing object. Use this before any operations that rely on the provided HPDF_Error instance.
requirements: error must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage of an HPDF_Error_Rec.
Must be called before other HPDF error API calls (Reset/GetCode/GetDetailCode/SetError/RaiseError) on the same HPDF_Error instance.
user_data may be NULL; it is stored and later passed to the error handler.

functions.name: HPDF_Error_Reset
functions.description: Clears the error state stored in the given HPDF_Error object, typically to reuse it after a previous error. Intended as a lightweight way to reset error_no/detail_no.
requirements: error must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid HPDF_Error_Rec (typically initialized via HPDF_Error_Init).

functions.name: HPDF_Error_GetCode
functions.description: Returns the primary error code currently stored in the HPDF_Error object. Useful for polling or inspecting the last error recorded for an operation.
requirements: error must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid HPDF_Error_Rec (typically initialized via HPDF_Error_Init).

functions.name: HPDF_Error_GetDetailCode
functions.description: Returns the detailed/subcode associated with the current error in the HPDF_Error object. The meaning of the detail code depends on the context of the error.
requirements: error must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid HPDF_Error_Rec (typically initialized via HPDF_Error_Init).

functions.name: HPDF_SetError
functions.signature: HPDF_STATUS HPDF_SetError(HPDF_Error error, HPDF_STATUS error_no, HPDF_STATUS detail_no);
functions.description: Sets the primary and detail error codes in the HPDF_Error object. Typically used internally by the library to record an error condition without immediately invoking an error handler. Returns a status code (exact return semantics are not documented here).
requirements: error must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid HPDF_Error_Rec (typically initialized via HPDF_Error_Init).
error_no should be a defined HPDF error/status code (e.g., one of the HPDF_* constants in this header).
detail_no should be a valid detail/status value for additional context; 0 may be used when no detail is available (inferred).
Callers should check the returned HPDF_STATUS to detect failure or propagate the error (exact semantics unknown; inferred from naming).

functions.name: HPDF_RaiseError
functions.signature: HPDF_STATUS HPDF_RaiseError(HPDF_Error error, HPDF_STATUS error_no, HPDF_STATUS detail_no);
functions.description: Records an error in the HPDF_Error object and raises it via the configured error handler. Intended to both set error_no/detail_no and notify the handler. Returns a status code (exact return semantics are not documented here).
requirements: error must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid HPDF_Error_Rec (typically initialized via HPDF_Error_Init).
error_no should be a defined HPDF error/status code (e.g., one of the HPDF_* constants in this header).
detail_no should be a valid detail/status value for additional context; 0 may be used when no detail is available (inferred).

May invoke the registered error handler; callers should be prepared for handler-defined behavior (e.g., logging or control-flow changes). The specific behavior is not defined in this header (inferred).

functions.name: HPDF_ExtGState_New
functions.description: Creates a new extended graphics state object (PDF ExtGState) within the Haru PDF library and returns it as a dictionary handle. Typically used to set up graphics parameters (e.g., transparency, blend modes) that can be applied to page content. Usage: supply a valid library memory manager and the document’s cross-reference table; store the returned dictionary and attach it to pages/resources as needed. Exact error signaling (e.g., null/invalid return on failure) is not documented here and is unknown.
requirements: mmgr must be a valid HPDF_MMgr obtained from the library; it must not be NULL (inferred from the parameter being a library handle).
xref must be a valid HPDF_Xref associated with the target document; it must not be NULL (inferred from the parameter being a library handle).
The returned HPDF_Dict must be treated as a library-managed object; life-cycle and ownership semantics are unknown from this header and should follow libharu conventions.
Callers should verify the return value before use; exact failure modes are unknown from this header.

functions.name: HPDF_ExtGState_Validate
functions.description: Validates an extended graphics state handle and returns a boolean indicating whether it represents a valid ExtGState object. Use this before operating on or attaching the object to ensure it is correctly constructed and usable.
requirements: ext_gstate must be an HPDF_ExtGState handle originating from this library (e.g., created via HPDF_ExtGState_New or retrieved from document structures).
Behavior when passing NULL or non-library pointers is not documented here; callers should avoid invalid handles.

functions.name: HPDF_Type1Font_New
functions.signature: HPDF_Font HPDF_Type1Font_New(HPDF_MMgr mmgr, HPDF_FontDef fontdef, HPDF_Encoder encoder, HPDF_Xref xref);
functions.description: Creates and returns a new Type1 font object for use in a PDF. Intended to be called with a Type1 font definition and an appropriate encoder within an active PDF/xref context. Returns a handle of type HPDF_Font (an HPDF_Dict). Exact error-reporting/ownership semantics are not documented in this header; typical usage is to check the returned handle before use.
requirements: mmgr must be a valid, initialized HPDF memory manager object (non-null).
fontdef must be a valid HPDF_FontDef corresponding to a Type1 font and initialized (non-null).
encoder must be a valid HPDF_Encoder compatible with the font/encoding you intend to use (non-null).
xref must be a valid HPDF_Xref associated with the current PDF document context (non-null).

Caller should check the returned HPDF_Font handle before use; specific failure mode (e.g., NULL on error) is not specified here and should be confirmed against the implementation or broader library docs.

functions.name: HPDF_TTFont_New
functions.signature: HPDF_Font HPDF_TTFont_New(HPDF_MMgr mmgr, HPDF_FontDef fontdef, HPDF_Encoder encoder, HPDF_Xref xref);
functions.description: Creates and returns a new TrueType font object for use in a PDF. Use with a TrueType font definition and a suitable encoder within an active PDF/xref context. Returns an HPDF_Font handle. Error signaling/ownership is not specified in this header; check the returned handle and consult implementation if needed.
requirements: mmgr must be a valid, initialized HPDF memory manager object (non-null).
fontdef must be a valid HPDF_FontDef describing a TrueType font and initialized (non-null).
encoder must be a valid HPDF_Encoder appropriate for the desired encoding of the TrueType font (non-null).
xref must be a valid HPDF_Xref for the active PDF document context (non-null).
Caller should verify the returned HPDF_Font handle before use; exact failure indicator is not documented here.

functions.name: HPDF_Type0Font_New
functions.signature: HPDF_Font HPDF_Type0Font_New(HPDF_MMgr mmgr, HPDF_FontDef fontdef, HPDF_Encoder encoder, HPDF_Xref xref);
functions.description: Creates and returns a new Type0 (composite) font object for use in a PDF. Typically used for CID-keyed composite fonts with multi-byte encodings; requires a matching font definition and encoder. Returns an HPDF_Font handle. Detailed error behavior and ownership are not documented in this header.
requirements: mmgr must be a valid, initialized HPDF memory manager (non-null).
fontdef must be a valid HPDF_FontDef appropriate for a Type0 (composite/CID) font and initialized (non-null).
encoder must be a valid HPDF_Encoder and should be compatible with multi-byte/CID encodings when applicable (non-null).
xref must be a valid HPDF_Xref associated with the current PDF document (non-null).
Caller should check the returned HPDF_Font handle before use; precise error signaling is not specified here.

functions.name: HPDF_Font_Validate
functions.description: Validates a font handle and returns whether it is usable/consistent. Intended to be called on an HPDF_Font obtained from the library to ensure it is a valid font dictionary before use in operations like text measurement or rendering. Specific validation criteria are not described in this header.
requirements: font must be a non-null HPDF_Font handle previously obtained from the library.
Caller should interpret the HPDF_BOOL result as success/failure; exact criteria for failure are not detailed here.

functions.name: HPDF_FontDef_Free
functions.description: Frees and destroys a font-definition object, releasing all associated resources. Call this when a HPDF_FontDef is no longer needed.
requirements: fontdef must be a valid HPDF_FontDef obtained from a corresponding constructor (e.g., HPDF_Type1FontDef_New, HPDF_TTFontDef_New, HPDF_CIDFontDef_New) or loader.
Do not use fontdef after this call (it becomes invalid).
Should not be called more than once on the same object.

functions.name: HPDF_FontDef_Cleanup
functions.description: Cleans up internal state of a font-definition object without destroying the object itself. Typically used to reset or release internal data prior to reuse or final free.
requirements: fontdef must be a valid, initialized HPDF_FontDef.
After cleanup, only operations that assume a cleaned/initialized state should be performed; details of what remains valid are unknown (not documented in this header).

functions.name: HPDF_FontDef_Validate
functions.description: Validates the font-definition object and returns whether it is in a usable/consistent state.
requirements: fontdef must be a valid HPDF_FontDef pointer.
Caller should check the returned HPDF_BOOL to decide if the font definition can be used; specific failure reasons are unknown from this header.

functions.name: HPDF_Type1FontDef_New
functions.description: Creates a new, empty Type 1 font-definition object using the provided memory manager.
requirements: mmgr must be a valid memory manager instance used by libharu.
Returned HPDF_FontDef must be freed with HPDF_FontDef_Free when no longer needed.

functions.name: HPDF_Type1FontDef_Load
functions.signature: HPDF_FontDef HPDF_Type1FontDef_Load(HPDF_MMgr mmgr, HPDF_Stream afm, HPDF_Stream font_data);
functions.description: Loads a Type 1 font definition from an AFM metrics stream and the corresponding font data stream, creating a ready-to-use font-definition object.
requirements: mmgr must be a valid memory manager.
afm must be a readable stream containing a valid AFM file.
font_data must be a readable stream containing the corresponding Type 1 font program (e.g., PFB/PFA); exact expected format is not specified here.
Returned HPDF_FontDef must be freed with HPDF_FontDef_Free.

functions.name: HPDF_Type1FontDef_Duplicate
functions.description: Creates a duplicate of an existing Type 1 font-definition object into the given memory manager.
requirements: mmgr must be valid.
src must be a valid Type 1 HPDF_FontDef.
Returned HPDF_FontDef must be freed with HPDF_FontDef_Free.

functions.name: HPDF_Type1FontDef_SetWidths
functions.description: Sets per-glyph widths for a Type 1 font definition using an array of HPDF_CharData entries.
requirements: fontdef must be a valid Type 1 font definition.
widths must point to a valid array of HPDF_CharData; the termination/length convention is unknown from this header (not documented).
Caller must check the returned HPDF_STATUS for success or failure.

functions.name: HPDF_Type1FontDef_GetWidthByName
functions.description: Returns the advance width for a glyph specified by its PostScript glyph name from a Type 1 font definition.
requirements: fontdef must be a valid Type 1 font definition.
glyph_name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated string naming a glyph present in the font.
Return value semantics for missing glyphs are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: HPDF_Type1FontDef_GetWidth
functions.description: Returns the advance width for the glyph mapped from the given Unicode code point in a Type 1 font definition.
requirements: fontdef must be a valid Type 1 font definition.
unicode must be a valid code point that maps to a glyph in the font; behavior for unmapped code points is not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: HPDF_Base14FontDef_New
functions.description: Creates a font-definition object for one of the PDF base 14 fonts by name (e.g., Times, Helvetica).
requirements: mmgr must be valid.
font_name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated string. It should correspond to a supported Base 14 font name; the accepted set and exact names are not specified here (unknown).
Returned HPDF_FontDef must be freed with HPDF_FontDef_Free.

functions.name: HPDF_TTFontDef_New
functions.description: Creates a new, empty TrueType font-definition object using the provided memory manager.
requirements: mmgr must be a valid memory manager.
Returned HPDF_FontDef must be freed with HPDF_FontDef_Free.

functions.name: HPDF_TTFontDef_Load
functions.signature: HPDF_FontDef HPDF_TTFontDef_Load(HPDF_MMgr mmgr, HPDF_Stream stream, HPDF_BOOL embedding);
functions.description: Loads a TrueType font from the given stream and creates a font-definition; supports controlling embedding via the embedding flag.
requirements: mmgr must be valid.
stream must be a readable stream positioned at a valid TrueType font.
embedding controls whether the font data may be embedded; exact policy/constraints are not specified here (unknown).
Returned HPDF_FontDef must be freed with HPDF_FontDef_Free.

functions.name: HPDF_TTFontDef_Load2
functions.signature: HPDF_FontDef HPDF_TTFontDef_Load2(HPDF_MMgr mmgr, HPDF_Stream stream, HPDF_UINT index, HPDF_BOOL embedding);
functions.description: Loads a TrueType or TrueType Collection (TTC) font from the given stream at the specified face index, creating a font-definition; embedding can be requested via flag.
requirements: mmgr must be valid.
stream must be a readable stream positioned at a valid TrueType font or TTC.
index must select a valid face within the collection when loading from TTC; valid range is not specified here (unknown).
embedding controls whether the font data may be embedded; exact policy/constraints are not specified here (unknown).
Returned HPDF_FontDef must be freed with HPDF_FontDef_Free.

functions.name: HPDF_TTFontDef_GetGlyphid
functions.description: Maps a Unicode code point to a glyph ID in the TrueType font definition and returns that glyph ID.
requirements: fontdef must be a valid TrueType font definition.
unicode must be a valid code point for which the font’s cmap may provide a mapping; behavior for unmapped characters is not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: HPDF_TTFontDef_GetCharWidth
functions.description: Returns the advance width for the glyph mapped from the given Unicode code point in a TrueType font definition.
requirements: fontdef must be a valid TrueType font definition.
unicode must be a valid code point; behavior for unmapped code points is not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: HPDF_TTFontDef_GetGidWidth
functions.description: Returns the advance width for the glyph with the specified glyph ID in a TrueType font definition.
requirements: fontdef must be a valid TrueType font definition.
gid must be a glyph ID within the font’s glyph range; exact valid range is not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: HPDF_TTFontDef_SaveFontData
functions.description: Writes or saves the font data associated with the TrueType font definition to the provided stream.
requirements: fontdef must be a valid TrueType font definition with accessible font data.
stream must be a writable stream; positioning/ownership semantics are not specified here (unknown).

functions.description: Formats the unsigned integer val into ASCII with a fixed width of len characters (likely zero-padded) and writes it to buffer s. Returns a char* (likely advanced pointer). Useful when a fixed-length numeric field is required.
requirements: s must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the output; the exact required size (including whether a null terminator is written) is not specified here and is unknown.
The formatting details (padding character, base) are not documented here and are unknown.

functions.name: HPDF_FToA
functions.signature: char* HPDF_FToA (char* s, HPDF_REAL val, char* eptr);
functions.description: Formats the floating-point value val into ASCII and writes it to the buffer starting at s, respecting eptr as an end/bounds pointer. Returns a char* (likely the next write position or s). Commonly used to serialize real numbers into PDF content safely within buffer limits.
requirements: s must point to a writable buffer.
eptr must point to the end boundary (past-the-last valid position) of the writable region and must be >= s.

The buffer between s and eptr must have sufficient space for the formatted number and any null terminator if one is written; the exact precision, formatting style, and return semantics are not documented here and are unknown.
Behavior on buffer exhaustion or special values (NaN/Inf) is not documented here and is unknown.

functions.name: HPDF_MemCpy
functions.signature: HPDF_BYTE* HPDF_MemCpy (HPDF_BYTE* out, const HPDF_BYTE* in, HPDF_UINT n);
functions.description: Copies n bytes from in to out. Equivalent in intent to memcpy; returns out.
requirements: out must point to a writable memory region of at least n bytes.
in must point to a readable memory region of at least n bytes.
Source and destination regions should not overlap; behavior for overlapping regions is unspecified.

functions.name: HPDF_StrCpy
functions.signature: HPDF_BYTE* HPDF_StrCpy (char* out, const char* in, char* eptr);
functions.description: Copies a C string from in to out, stopping at eptr boundary. Intended as a bounded string copy that avoids overruns by respecting eptr as the end pointer. Returns a pointer (HPDF_BYTE*) to some position in the destination (likely the next write position).
requirements: out must point to a writable buffer.
in must be a readable, null-terminated C string unless copying stops due to eptr; detailed truncation behavior is unknown.
eptr must point to the end boundary (past-the-last valid position) of the writable region and must be >= out.
Behavior when the string does not fit (e.g., truncation, null-termination) is not documented here and is unknown.

functions.name: HPDF_MemCmp
functions.signature: HPDF_INT HPDF_MemCmp (const HPDF_BYTE* s1, const HPDF_BYTE* s2, HPDF_UINT n);
functions.description: Lexicographically compares the first n bytes of s1 and s2, similar to memcmp. Returns an integer less than, equal to, or greater than zero depending on the comparison.
requirements: s1 and s2 must each point to readable memory regions of at least n bytes.

functions.name: HPDF_StrCmp
functions.signature: HPDF_INT HPDF_StrCmp (const char* s1, const char* s2);
functions.description: Compares two null-terminated C strings, similar to strcmp. Returns an integer indicating ordering or equality.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be readable, null-terminated C strings.

functions.name: HPDF_StrStr
functions.signature: const char* HPDF_StrStr (const char* s1, const char* s2, HPDF_UINT maxlen);
functions.description: Searches for the first occurrence of substring s2 within s1, scanning at most maxlen bytes of s1. Returns a pointer to the first match or possibly NULL if not found.
requirements: s1 must point to a readable memory region of at least maxlen bytes; if s1 is shorter, it must still be readable up to its terminator.
s2 must be a readable, null-terminated C string.
Behavior when s2 is empty, or return value NULL vs. non-NULL specifics, is not documented here and is inferred.

functions.name: HPDF_MemSet
functions.signature: void* HPDF_MemSet (void* s, HPDF_BYTE c, HPDF_UINT n);
functions.description: Fills n bytes of the buffer at s with the byte value c, analogous to memset. Returns s.
requirements: s must point to a writable memory region of at least n bytes.

functions.name: HPDF_StrLen
functions.signature: HPDF_UINT HPDF_StrLen (const char* s, HPDF_INT maxlen);
functions.description: Computes the length of string s up to a maximum of maxlen characters, similar to strnlen. Returns the number of characters examined before a null terminator or maxlen is reached.
requirements: s must be a readable C string; it may be unterminated if maxlen limits the scan.
maxlen specifies the maximum number of bytes to examine; behavior for negative values is not documented here and is unknown.

functions.name: HPDF_ToBox
functions.signature: HPDF_Box HPDF_ToBox (HPDF_INT16 left, HPDF_INT16 bottom, HPDF_INT16 right, HPDF_INT16 top);
functions.description: Constructs and returns an HPDF_Box structure from the given edge coordinates.
requirements: No special runtime requirements; callers should supply coordinates in the library's expected units and ordering.

functions.name: HPDF_ToPoint
functions.description: Constructs and returns an HPDF_Point structure from the provided coordinates.
requirements: No special runtime requirements; callers should supply coordinates in the library's expected units.

functions.name: HPDF_ToRect
functions.signature: HPDF_Rect HPDF_ToRect (HPDF_REAL left, HPDF_REAL bottom, HPDF_REAL right, HPDF_REAL top);
functions.description: Constructs and returns an HPDF_Rect structure from the given edge coordinates using real-valued inputs.
requirements: No special runtime requirements; callers should supply coordinates in the library's expected units and ordering.

functions.name: HPDF_UInt16Swap
functions.description: Swaps the byte order of the 16-bit unsigned integer pointed to by value (endianness swap) in place.
requirements: value must be a non-null pointer to a writable HPDF_UINT16.

functions.name: HPDF_PDFA_AppendOutputIntents
functions.signature: HPDF_STATUS HPDF_PDFA_AppendOutputIntents(HPDF_Doc pdf, const char *iccname, HPDF_Dict iccdict);
functions.description: Appends a PDF/A OutputIntent dictionary to the document using the provided ICC profile dictionary and profile name. Intended to embed/declare color profile information required by PDF/A conformance. Call when preparing a PDF/A document to associate an output ICC profile.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle and must not be NULL.
iccname must be a valid, null-terminated string pointer and must not be NULL.
iccdict must be a valid HPDF_Dict referencing an ICC profile object; must not be NULL.
Caller should check the returned HPDF_STATUS and handle non-success codes appropriately (exact error codes are library-defined).
Function should be called only when the document is in a modifiable state (i.e., before the document is finalized/saved).
Ownership of iccname and iccdict remains with the caller unless otherwise documented elsewhere (no ownership transfer implied by this signature).

functions.name: HPDF_PDFA_SetPDFAConformance
functions.description: Sets the target PDF/A conformance level for the document (e.g., PDF/A-1a, PDF/A-1b, etc., as represented by HPDF_PDFAType). Intended for configuring the document so subsequent operations adhere to the selected PDF/A profile.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle and must not be NULL.
pdfatype must be a valid HPDF_PDFAType enumeration value.
Caller must check the returned HPDF_STATUS and handle errors.
Should be called when configuring the document, typically before saving; exact timing requirements relative to other calls are not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: HPDF_PDFA_AddXmpMetadata
functions.description: Adds required XMP metadata to the document for PDF/A compliance. This typically inserts or updates the document’s XMP packet with minimum mandatory PDF/A schemas.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle and must not be NULL.
Caller must check the returned HPDF_STATUS and handle errors.
Should be called before finalizing/saving the document so that the metadata is included (exact ordering relative to other metadata operations is not specified in this header).

functions.name: HPDF_PDFA_AddXmpExtension
functions.description: Registers or appends a custom XMP schema/extension described by the provided description string to the document’s XMP metadata for PDF/A usage. Useful for declaring additional namespaces and properties beyond the base PDF/A schemas.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle and must not be NULL.

xmp_description must be a valid, null-terminated string pointer and must not be NULL. Expected to contain a properly formatted XMP extension description; exact format is not specified in this header (unknown).
Caller must check the returned HPDF_STATUS and handle errors.
Call before finalizing/saving the document for the extension to be embedded.

functions.name: HPDF_PDFA_ClearXmpExtensions
functions.description: Clears any XMP extension schemas that were previously registered for the document. Useful to reset or remove queued extensions before finalizing the document’s XMP metadata.
requirements: pdf must be a valid, initialized HPDF_Doc handle and must not be NULL.
Should be called before finalizing/saving the document; effect on already-written metadata after save is undefined (unknown).

functions.name: HPDF_PDFA_GenerateID
functions.description: Generates and assigns a PDF/A-compliant document ID to the document (e.g., updates the document’s ID array). Intended to ensure required identifiers are present for PDF/A compliance.
requirements: The HPDF_Doc argument must be a valid, initialized document handle and must not be NULL.
Caller must check the returned HPDF_STATUS and handle errors.
Call before finalizing/saving the document so the ID is embedded.

functions.name: HPDF_3DC3DMeasure_New
functions.signature: HPDF_3DMeasure HPDF_3DC3DMeasure_New(HPDF_MMgr mmgr, HPDF_Xref xref, HPDF_Point3D firstanchorpoint, HPDF_Point3D textanchorpoint);
functions.description: Creates a new 3D measurement object (C3D measure) in a Haru PDF document. The function allocates/initializes an HPDF_3DMeasure associated with the given memory manager and cross-reference table, using the supplied 3D points for the first anchor and the text anchor. Typical usage is to construct a 3D measurement annotation/entry that can be attached to or embedded within a 3D annotation. Specific semantics of the C3D measure subtype and how the points are interpreted are not documented in this header and remain unknown.
requirements: mmgr must be a valid, initialized memory manager handle (HPDF_MMgr).
xref must be a valid, initialized cross-reference table handle (HPDF_Xref) corresponding to the target document.
firstanchorpoint must be a valid 3D point (HPDF_Point3D) in the expected coordinate space for the 3D content; exact coordinate system is unspecified here (unknown).
textanchorpoint must be a valid 3D point (HPDF_Point3D); the exact role and constraints (e.g., must not coincide with other points) are not documented (unknown).
The function returns an HPDF_3DMeasure handle or an error via the library’s usual error mechanism; exact error reporting/return-on-failure behavior is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: HPDF_PD33DMeasure_New
functions.signature: HPDF_3DMeasure HPDF_PD33DMeasure_New(HPDF_MMgr mmgr, HPDF_Xref xref, HPDF_Point3D annotationPlaneNormal, HPDF_Point3D firstAnchorPoint, HPDF_Point3D secondAnchorPoint, HPDF_Point3D leaderLinesDirection, HPDF_Point3D measurementValuePoint, HPDF_Point3D textYDirection, HPDF_REAL value, const char* unitsString);
functions.description: Creates a new 3D measurement object (likely a point-to-point/PD3 3D measure) with explicit geometric parameters. The function associates the measure with the provided memory manager and xref, using vectors/points that define the annotation plane normal, two anchor points to measure between, the leader line direction, a point indicating where the measurement value applies, the text’s Y direction, and a numeric measurement value with an accompanying units string. Intended for constructing detailed 3D measurement annotations within a 3D PDF context. Exact semantics of each vector/point and how the value/units are used are not documented in this header and remain partially unknown.
requirements: mmgr must be a valid, initialized memory manager handle (HPDF_MMgr).
xref must be a valid, initialized cross-reference table handle (HPDF_Xref) for the target document.
annotationPlaneNormal should be a valid 3D direction vector; normalization requirements are not stated (unknown).
firstAnchorPoint and secondAnchorPoint must be valid 3D points; ordering and non-degeneracy constraints are not stated (unknown).
leaderLinesDirection should be a valid 3D direction vector; normalization and orthogonality constraints are not stated (unknown).
measurementValuePoint must be a valid 3D point; its relation to other geometry is not specified (unknown).
textYDirection should be a valid 3D direction vector for labeling orientation; normalization is not specified (unknown).
value is an HPDF_REAL numeric value; acceptable ranges or special values (e.g., negative, NaN) are not specified (unknown).
unitsString must be a pointer to a null-terminated C string; encoding and allowed contents are not specified here (unknown).
The function returns an HPDF_3DMeasure handle or an error via the library’s usual error mechanism; exact failure/return conventions are not detailed in this header (unknown).

functions.name: HPDF_3DAnnotExData_New
functions.description: Creates a new extended data (ExData) object for a 3D annotation within a PDF document. Intended to be used when constructing or attaching 3D annotation-specific data that will be recorded in the document’s cross-reference table. Typical usage is to call this with a valid library memory manager and the document’s xref, then attach the returned ExData to a 3D annotation via other library APIs. Return-value/error semantics are not documented in this header; consult library docs or check for a valid handle before use.
requirements: mmgr must be a valid, initialized HPDF_MMgr instance provided by the library (inferred from naming and type).
xref must be a valid HPDF_Xref associated with the target PDF document (inferred from naming and type).
Both mmgr and xref must be non-NULL before calling (general library convention; not stated explicitly).

Caller must verify that the returned HPDF_ExData handle is valid before using it; exact failure indication (e.g., NULL or error state) is not specified in this header and should be handled per library conventions.
